Question: I joined Quora 12 days ago, I have asked 347 questions and this will be my 348th question. What should I do?
Answer: Stop wasting everyone's time, including your own. Delete your Quora account, walk away from it and don't look back, not even to make sure that it's gone; if you do, Quora will think you've changed your mind, and will cancel the deletion. Then go away and develop a real life, one that doesn't involve Quora.

Question: In the novel Pride and Prejudice, by Jane Austen, why is Lady Catherine de Bourgh styled 'the Right Honourable', a style borne by privy counsellors and by peers beneath the rank of marquess?
Answer: Possibly for the same reason that Dr Samuel Johnson gave, when asked how he came to give a distinctly inaccurate definition for the word “pastern,” instead of “fetlock,” in his famous dictionary: “Ignorance, Ma'am, pure ignorance!” he said airily. Well, he didn't need to know much about horses. Jane Austen was many things, but I don't think an expert on constitutional or political matters was one of them. Honourables are frequently younger sons of baronets, these days, but that wasn't always the case, and during the 18th and 19th centuries use of The Honourable and Right Honourable changed quite a lot. So Jane might have been wrong, but not necessarily. There's an interesting Britannica article here, which is too long, and covers too many meanings, to be summarised quickly or easily. I can only suggest that you read it for yourself, John, and see what you make of it!

Question: What's the average age of first time mothers?
Answer: It's impossible to answer this truthfully and simply, because it depends on the part of the world where you live, and changes over time. When I had my first baby, I was 28, and the medical profession in the UK classed me as an “elderly primigravida,” ie old for a first-time mum. Two other ladies gave birth the same evening; both were a farmer's wife, both were 40, and both had a baby boy. One was having a fourth attempt at producing a son for her husband to leave the farm to, but for the other it was a first baby. The nursing staff thought having babies at their age was quite amazing. Those babies are all now in their 40s. Now, 28 is no longer considered “elderly” for having first babies, and first babies at 40+ are no longer unusual. And it has its points. For many years it's been said that the ideal time for giving birth is when you're about 17. However, the best age for bringing up babies and children was said to be in your 40s. It seemed that the answer was for young daughters to produce the babies, and then let Mum and Dad bring them up, while the young couple lived, worked, and earned the necessary money to pay for things. But now that so many women of 40 are having babies, Mum and Dad can do the babysitting in their 60s!

Question: Do you think that the grade boundaries will go up or down this year for GCSEs?
Answer: Yes, definitely. They always do! I get asked this every year, and the answer is always basically the same. It will vary from exam board to exam board, subject to subject, and paper to paper, just as it always does, and nobody will know until all the exam scripts for that paper have been marked. This too is always true. With the best will in the world, however hard the examiners try, the standard of the paper will vary, being harder some years, and easier in others; they don't mean it to be, but that's what seems to happen. They're not really aware of this until they can see how difficult, or how easy, students found it. So, because the examiners want to keep the standard of grades consistent, if it turns out that students found it pretty easy, the grade boundaries will have to go up a bit until the gradings feel right to the experienced teachers who are also the examiners. And in the same way, if it's clear that students struggled, then the boundaries will have to go down a bit. A true Grade 5 student, or Grade 9 student or whatever, should get that grade whenever they take the exam, however easy or hard it was. And that's how it works, and why I can't answer your question with a nice straightforward Yes or No!
